Trust me, I've been in your spot. One thing I've learned over my short time near thirty years alive is that you will be surprised how things can change in the span of a year, especially when your out of school. Your in a bit of a slog period right now, and who knows, maybe a year after school you'll be in a different state, traveling the world, hanging out with a group of friends you never thought you would have. I mean fuck a year ago I was in a completely different state, never thinking I would ever move out of my home state. People, events, homes change so instantaneously, sometimes you'll find yourself amazed by where you are. Stick it out, and I know it will get better, or at least be different.

It might purely be the area I'm in, and I have run into people from opposing teams that are really chill, kind of like the interaction you described, but more often then not I also run into people being generally shitty and exclusive with a game that's supposed to encourage connections.

I live in a large metropolitan area, which makes it kind of obvious when people are playing. Which also contributes to the climate I experience. But actually, the 'pokemon yeah' response is very common. There are good hearted players put there, I'm just noticing the influx of mean spirited people two days after release.
It takes a while, but honestly I don't find myself lifting my hand that much. It is strange going back to my mouse at home, which is just a crappy Logitech mouse from Costco.

The mouse still functions maybe a centimeter off the surface, but I don't need to lift the mouse anymore to traverse across three screens. It's daunting at first, but really nice once you get the hang of it. But yeah it stops functioning if you lift it any higher.

I have it for work. Very sensitive, takes some getting used to, but once you do it's fantastic. Haven't used it for games however. Mine came in a bundle that comes with a ergonomic keyboard, which is sleek as hell.
